rationale: CR-001 through CR-004 verified resolved in source: notice level now flows through types.ts/parser.ts/filter.ts/formatter.ts (CR-001), executor.ts's new notifiedFailedHooks dedup stops console flooding on repeat hook failures (CR-002), logger.ts's notice() now spreads sanitized args into console.warn (CR-003), and vitest.config.ts's testCodemieHome is now PID-suffixed as the finding's own recommendation offered (CR-004). The CR-002 fix itself introduces a new defect: clearCache() (executor.ts:545-547) never clears notifiedFailedHooks, so a hook's console notice is permanently silenced after its first failure even for a later, different error — filed as CR-005 (major/patch), which forces request-changes. Confidence is medium: three resolutions are unambiguous but CR-004 only closes the cross-invocation race, not the intra-run parallel-worker race the finding also named, and CR-005 shows the confirmation pass still catching new gaps.

findings.title: notifiedFailedHooks never cleared, silences repeat failures
findings.problem: clearCache() (executor.ts:545-547) clears executedHooks but not notifiedFailedHooks. executeSingleHook's catch block (executor.ts:404-410) downgrades every failure of a given hook to logger.warn() (file-log only, no console) once that hook's hash has failed once, and nothing ever removes a hash from notifiedFailedHooks for the life of the HookExecutor instance.
findings.impact: The CR-002 fix (added to stop the console from flooding on every failed tool call) overshoots: instead of rate-limiting repeats of the same underlying failure, it permanently silences the console notice for that hook — even a later, unrelated error from the same hook (e.g. a different script bug after the first is fixed) is written to the file log but never surfaced on the terminal, defeating the guaranteed-visibility purpose of the notice level this task set out to add.
findings.recommendation: Clear notifiedFailedHooks in clearCache() alongside executedHooks (or key the dedup on (hookHash, event cycle) instead of instance lifetime) so a hook gets a fresh console notice per event cycle, or per distinct error, rather than being silenced forever after its first failure.

finding_status.notes: types.ts:8 LogLevel now includes 'notice'; parser.ts:68 normalizeLogLevel branches to 'notice'; filter.ts:41 LogFilterEngine.byLevel maps notice:2 (surfaces under --level warn and above); formatter.ts:67 formatLevel colors notice yellow alongside warn. The console-visibility/classification defect described in CR-001 is fixed; index.ts's --level help text (line 23) and type cast (line 361) weren't updated to mention 'notice' but this is a stale-documentation gap, not a functional block (byLevel already keys on the runtime string).

executor.ts:56 adds notifiedFailedHooks; executor.ts:404-410's catch block now calls logger.notice() only on a hook's first tracked failure and logger.warn() (no console output) on every repeat of that same hook hash, preventing console flooding from a hook that fails on every tool call.

logger.ts:354 notice() now builds sanitizedArgs via sanitizeLogArgs(...args) and spreads them into console.warn(chalk.yellow(...), ...sanitizedArgs), matching writeToLogFile's handling; extra args are no longer dropped from the console channel.

vitest.config.ts:12 now computes testCodemieHome as join(tmpdir(), `codemie-test-home-${process.pid}`), giving each vitest invocation its own directory — the 'per-worker/per-PID suffix' option the original finding's own recommendation offered — closing the concrete cross-invocation collision risk. The intra-run parallel-worker scenario the finding also named (workers within one run still share this per-run path) is not separately addressed, but was already assessed in the prior round as an unconfirmed, not a demonstrated, collision.
